chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who accuses another man of zina, then the latter pardons him and releases him from that, but afterward it appears proper to him to bring him forward so that the hadd be carried out for him. He said: “There is no hadd upon him after the pardon.”

I said: What if he says, “O son of a fornicatress,” and he pardons him and leaves that for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? He said: “If his mother is alive, then he has no right to pardon; the pardon belongs to his mother. Whenever she wishes, she may claim her right. But if his mother has died, then he is the guardian of her affair, and his pardon is valid.”

key_terms.فَيَعْفُو: to pardon or forgo one’s claim
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: released from liability or absolved of the claim
key_terms.وَلِيُّ أَمْرِهَا: the one who holds authority over her legal claim after her death
key_terms.يَا ٱبْنَ ٱلزَّانِيَةِ: an insult imputing illicit sexual conduct to one’s mother
key_terms.ٱلزِّنَى: illicit sexual intercourse, the charge at issue in qadhf

ai.seo_question: Can the hadd for qadhf be enforced after the offended person has already pardoned the offender?
ai.summary: This hadith explains legal rulings concerning qadhf and insulting lineage. It states that once a victim of accusation of zina pardons the offender, the hadd is no longer pursued; but when the insult concerns the mother, the right of pardon belongs to her if she is alive, and to her heir or guardian if she has died.
